Dear all,
This PR addresses the issue described [here](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/issues/687), where the parallel world geometry was affecting the reconstruction due to overlapping materials. Cheers,  
Andrea

data.author: jmcarcell
data.body:

The regression test checks both seed input types: four assertions fail with the old lookup, and all pass with the handle lookup. All 17 unit tests passed locally (and failed before the changes).

A study now owns its trials. Until now Optuna's journal or database held them: their numbers and states, the record each was told, rejections, recovery marks and the parent/child links of nested studies. `load_study`, recovery and the nested scheduler all read Optuna objects.

data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES

- `ACTSDuplicateRemoval` no longer keeps two equal tracks (more than half of the hits of the shorter one shared). A track is now dropped if an equal kept track is at least as good, and otherwise replaces all equal kept tracks.

ENDRELEASENOTES

Two ways the old loop kept duplicates:

- a better track replaced the *first* equal kept track and stopped, so further kept tracks equal to it stayed;
- a worse track did not stop at the first equal one and could replace a later one, so the kept list then held two tracks equal to each other.

This happens when partial tracks of one particle are around (they are not equal to each other, but both are equal to the full track): two full copies can each replace one of them and both survive.

data.title: fix(env): set LD_LIBRARY_PATH also on macOS
data.author: wdconinc
data.body:
Although macOS doesn't use `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, ROOT still uses it, and with precedence over `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` (https://github.com/root-project/root/blob/v6-40-02/interpreter/cling/lib/Interpreter/DynamicLibraryManager.cpp#L30-L56). That means that a compilation in an environment with an existing DD4hep (such as LCG in CI), the existing DD4hep will be picked up by cling before the version loaded by `thisdd4hep.sh`. That's a consequence of LCG's views where the `setup.sh` adds the view/lib to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

This PR just makes sure that we then also add (prepend) this DD4hep before the one in the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` already.

Maybe the real issue here is that ROOT shouldn't look in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` at all on macOS but we can't change that.

data.title: DDCore: use std::call_once for threadsafe MultipoleField initialization
data.author: wdconinc
data.body:
MultipoleField previously used a thread-unsafe boolean flag, which led to data races during multithreaded running:
- one thread would get into the if block and immediately set the flag,
- the next thread would stay out of the if block and assume initialization had already happened,
- only then would the first thread complete initialization.

This results in incorrect fields in the second thread (for the first event only).

This PR converts to using call_once on a private initialize function (see `SurfaceManager` for this approach). Most of the diff is just indentation correction.

BEGINRELEASENOTES
- DDCore: use std::call_once for threadsafe MultipoleField initialization

ENDRELEASENOTES

data.title: fix(DDG4): create sensitive detectors in reproducible order
data.author: wdconinc
data.body:
`Geant4GeometryInfo::sensitives` is a `std::map` keyed on `SensitiveDetector` handles, which are [compared by pointer](https://github.com/AIDASoft/DD4hep/blob/7693cca27dd057bb22414c86b95fedbab49f6ae5/DDCore/include/DD4hep/Handle.h#L118).
